claim.why_it_matters: The row label 'CJK Unified Ideographs:' is split: 'CJK Unified' is a stray paragraph and the row (now the table's header row) is labelled only 'Ideographs:', so the classification name is lost from the row.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page (2014 p.768, PDF page 792, Annex B.3.1) sets the label on two lines: 'CJK Unified' on the first line and 'Ideographs:' on the second, with the code-point ranges beside the second line. The markdown keeps both words in order, on the line directly before the table row: 'CJK Unified' as a paragraph, then the row '| Ideographs: | 3400-4DB5, ... FA27-FA29 |'. Every code point matches the PDF. No text is missing and no range is attached to the wrong script. The difference is a two-line label wrapped across a table boundary, plus markdown table scaffolding (the row becoming a header row). That is reflow and formatting. A reader still sees 'CJK Unified' next to 'Ideographs:' and its ranges, so the meaning is unchanged. The rejection criteria cover this case: the text is present on an adjacent line and the difference is only line wrapping or formatting.
